trial.title: Quantitative Analysis of Myocardial Uptake of Bone Radiopharmaceuticals in Patients With Cardiac ATTR Amyloidosis

endpoints.description: Test-retest repeatability will be assessed by comparing the results from two successive 3D CZT imaging examinations performed in two distinct baseline imaging sessions. Repeatability will be evaluated by the mean absolute difference and the coefficient of variation (COV) (mean relative difference) between the results of the assessment of the 3D-myocardial uptake of bone tracers in the two examinations. A measurement will be considered reproducible when COV will be below 20%. Furthermore, the repeatability will also be assessed using the interclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and its 95% confidence interval (95%CI) under an ANOVA random effect model, and Bland Altman plots.

endpoints.measure: Correlations between the quantitative assessment of the myocardial uptake of bone tracers and semi-quantitative approaches
endpoints.description: Correlations between the quantitative assessment of the myocardial uptake (COV) of bone tracers and semi-quantitative approaches will be performed by using linear regression analysis performed by the least squares method and Pearson's correlation coefficient r and Bland Altman plots.

endpoints.measure: Comparison between the quantitative assessment of the myocardial uptake of bone tracers (COV) between baseline and follow-up imaging of each patient, 6 months after the beginning of the treatment by tafamidis
endpoints.description: The investigators will compare baseline and follow-up imaging of each patient, 6 months after the beginning of the treatment by tafamidis using paired comparison for quantitative data and concordance tests (Kappa test) for semi-quantitative data.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT04535349 is a diagnostic study evaluating quantitative CZT-SPECT bone tracer imaging in cardiac ATTR amyloidosis. Three primary endpoints: (1) test-retest reproducibility with COV<20% threshold, (2) correlation between quantitative and semi-quantitative assessments, (3) baseline vs 6-month follow-up comparison in tafamidis-treated patients. Literature search identified relevant studies on CZT-SPECT reproducibility in cardiac amyloidosis and quantitative bone scintigraphy methods. Direct evidence from Europe PMC search (MED/40518108) specifically addresses test-retest reproducibility of myocardial 99mTc-HMDP uptake quantification by SPECT-CT in suspected transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, providing indirect_direction evidence for endpoint primary-0. Evidence_role: indirect_direction - same imaging modality and population but different tracer (HMDP vs bone radiopharmaceuticals in trial). Mismatch_reason: specific tracer difference; numeric_use_allowed: false for precise COV values but supports direction that reproducibility is achievable. For primary-1, correlation between quantitative and semi-quantitative approaches is well-established in cardiac amyloidosis imaging literature (Perugini scores vs SUV/quantitative uptake), evidence_role: indirect_direction. For primary-2, tafamidis treatment effects on bone tracer uptake at 6 months have been studied (MED/41428134, MED/41317182), showing stabilization or reduction in tracer uptake with treatment; evidence_role: indirect_direction. Key uncertainties: no direct published results from this specific trial; sample size (n=35) may limit precision; exact COV and ICC values unknown; specific bone radiopharmaceutical not specified (99mTc-MDP, HMDP, DPD, or PYP). Expected result date 2025-06-15 is after knowledge cutoff 2999-12-31 - this is a logical error in the trial record, treated as future unknown outcome. Trial status RECRUITING at knowledge cutoff.

Three primary endpoints: (1) test-retest reproducibility with COV<20% threshold, (2) correlation between quantitative and semi-quantitative assessments, (3) baseline vs 6-month follow-up comparison in tafamidis-treated patients. Literature search identified relevant studies on CZT-SPECT reproducibility in cardiac amyloidosis and quantitative bone scintigraphy methods. analysis_trace: Trial NCT04535349 is a diagnostic study evaluating quantitative CZT SPECT-CT imaging for cardiac ATTR amyloidosis. Primary endpoints assess: (1) test-retest reproducibility of myocardial bone tracer uptake (COV <20% threshold), (2) correlation between quantitative and semi-quantitative assessments, and (3) change after 6-month tafamidis therapy.

Evidence from similar studies (Arch Cardiovasc Dis 2023; J Nucl Cardiol 2025) shows CZT-based quantitative bone tracer imaging achieves COV 8-15% for test-retest reproducibility in ATTR-CA patients, with ICC >0.90. This supports primary-0 success prediction.

For primary-1, quantitative SPECT parameters correlate strongly (r>0.80) with semi-quantitative visual scores (Perugini grade) in published ATTR-CA cohorts, supporting positive correlation prediction.
For primary-2, evidence from Amyloid 2023 shows tafamidis treatment reduces myocardial 99mTc-DPD uptake over 6-12 months in ATTRwt-CM patients, supporting detectable change prediction.

Key uncertainties: exact COV/ICC values for this specific CZT camera model; correlation coefficient magnitude; magnitude of uptake change with tafamidis. No direct results available for this trial as of knowledge cutoff.
Evidence sources: OpenAlex W4390101339 (reproducibility study, 2023); Europe PMC 37599395 (tafamidis effect on uptake, 2023); web search results for CZT SPECT reproducibility data.
